headline: Seven of seven majors above their 200-day lines with momentum flat, while BTC sees conflicting flows and shorts flush in altcoins
paragraphs: The regime is bullish on the tape. All seven majors sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and six of them (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, and DOGE) have completed golden crosses, meaning the 50-day has crossed above the 200-day. Only ADA, the laggard, has neither the cross nor the trend line beneath it. That breadth is the first thing: when the whole board is above the long-term trend, the floor is higher than it was. Bitcoin is 36.8% down from its 12-month high of $124,740, Ethereum is 45.6% down, and Solana is 58.2% down, yet they sit in an uptrend. Distance from a high is not a signal by itself; it is only a measure of how much ground has been given back.

Momentum tells a different story. Every single major asset, from BTC through ADA, has its MACD below its signal line. That means the rate of change is not accelerating; the move is cooling. RSI readings sit in the 51 to 64 range, which is neutral to slightly hot but nowhere near overbought. BTC at 59.7 and SOL at 58.7 are the closest to midline; ETH at 63.7 and XRP at 61.1 are a touch firmer. This is a resting trend, not a sprinting one. The 30-day realized volatility is high across the board (ETH at 71.6%, XRP at 91.9%, SOL at 67.3%), which means price is swinging hard in both directions even as the trend holds. This is momentum divergence: the major moves are up on the month (BTC up 24.1%, ETH up 35.6%, SOL up 40.7%), yet the daily engine is cool.

Positioning in derivatives shows what the market is paying for. Bitcoin and Ethereum are moderately funded at 0.004% per eight hours (4.4% annualized), a level that leans long but is not expensive. Solana, XRP, and DOGE are twice as hot at 0.01% per eight hours (11% annualized), meaning longs are paying to hold those bets. Open interest on BTC is $2.08 billion and on ETH is $1.54 billion, substantial pools. The long-to-short ratio on BTC is 1.22 and on ETH is 1.26, meaning the market is biased long but not crowded; DOGE, by contrast, is 4.32 longs for every short, a tail-end positioning extreme. Liquidations over the last two hours in BTC were 100 fills: $274,846 in longs, $1,529,320 in shorts. The shorts are washing out faster than the longs, which is consistent with a bid underneath the market, though the sample is small.

Flows show a market in transition. On the day of September 14, BTC ETF spot flows printed a small inflow of $9.7 million. Over the last five sessions, however, the net is a $453 million outflow. This disagreement says the selling pressure is not new and not fading in the five-day window. ETH is the opposite: inflow of $216.4 million on the day of September 11 and a five-session net inflow of $222.8 million, so the bid from traditional finance is consistent. Stablecoin float stands at $310.1 billion, up 1.25% in the last 30 days, which is dry powder but not a pile of fresh ammunition. Whale flows over the last 72 hours show $5 million net moving onto exchanges, and the biggest moves are USDC onto Kraken ($170.8 million) and USDT onto Binance ($157.1 million), the classic setup for a sale. Yet over the week ending September 14, that same whale flow reverses: $725 million moved onto exchanges in the most recent week, but the week ending September 7 saw $347 million move off exchanges. The pattern is choppy, with net inflow in three of the last four weeks, suggesting institutions are rotating or hedging rather than capitulating.

Sentiment reads as Greed at 57, which sits in the middle of its 30-day range of 31 to 74. The crowd is neither panicked nor euphoric. The tape underneath does not gainsay this: the rally on the month is real (24% for BTC, 35% for ETH, 40% for SOL), but momentum is flat, positioning is firm but not unsafe, and flows are mixed. Altcoins outside the seven majors are moving harder; PONS is up 17.55% in 24 hours and PENDLE is up 15.1%, while losers like FF are down 10.58%. The dispersion tells you the bid is selective, not across the board.

Watch for three conditions that would change the picture. First, a funding flip: if BTC and ETH funding moves from positive to negative, longs stop paying and shorts begin to profit, which would signal a momentum turn. Second, a loss of the 200-day line on the major trend assets; a drop below that level on four or more would break the regime. Third, a sustained reversal in ETF flows: if the five-session net on BTC flips to inflow and holds, traditional finance is buying the dip, which would contradict the narrative of institutional rotation.
